messages:
Jordan: Hey all — first day WSL + Docker setup. My kubectl contexts seem to flip between clusters when I open VS Code terminals. I also see errors like "Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp ... timed out". I think Docker Desktop altered my KUBECONFIG pointing at a kubeconfig managed by Docker. What's the recommended pattern so I don't accidentally operate in prod? Who should I ask for namespace access?

Priya: welcome! :wave: A few quick checks: 1) check what kubectl sees: `kubectl config get-contexts` and `kubectl config current-context` 2) check env var: `echo $KUBECONFIG` — WSL/Windows path translation can be weird (use `wslpath -w` if needed) 3) make a per-user merged config in WSL: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/docker-desktop kubectl config view --merge --flatten > ~/.kube/merged && mv ~/.kube/merged ~/.kube/config` 4) pin VS Code terminal to use the WSL distro (not PowerShell) so it doesn't pull the Windows kubeconfig. If you want to avoid merges, keep Docker Desktop's kubeconfig at `~/.kube/docker-desktop` and set `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config` in `~/.profile`.

Alex: also to avoid accidental prod ops, we use namespace-level RBAC. For dev access submit a request via https://access.redwood.internal (choose 'Kubernetes namespace access'). We'll then create a RoleBinding like: ```kubectl create rolebinding jordan-dev-binding --clusterrole=edit --user=jordan@redwood.com --namespace=dev``` If you need service account access for CI, message me and I'll provision one.

onboard-bot: Welcome Jordan! To speed this up, please fill the 'K8s access' form: https://onboard.redwood.internal/k8s and include your WSL distro name and desired namespaces.

Jordan: Thanks — followed Priya's steps, exported KUBECONFIG and set it in ~/.profile; confirmed `kubectl config current-context` shows my dev cluster only. Filed the access form for the 'dev' namespace. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
